interpretation: Quarter and half exposure decodes show the expected linear scaling in ordinary channels. Dividing the quarter-exposure decode by 0.25 restores the shared normalization while retaining real RGB values above 1; the unshifted rendering clips some of these channels. This is a LibRaw offline rendering comparison, not a different camera capture or a sensor highlight reconstruction.

rendering_formulas.baseline: standard sRGB transfer applied after clipping scene * exposure to [0,1]
rendering_formulas.protected: max-channel knee=0.5; target peak=0.5+0.5*(p-0.5)/(0.5+(p-0.5)) above knee; uniformly scale RGB to target peak; blend this linear RGB with the ordinarily clipped scene using strength, then standard sRGB transfer
rendering_formulas.recipe: gains=exp([warmth+tint/2,-tint,-warmth+tint/2]); normalize gains to weighted sum 1 with [0.2126,0.7152,0.0722]; multiply already-WB linear sRGB and render_protected strength=0.7

limitations: Offline experiment, not a camera-verified JPEG engine or a new capture exposure.
Sensor-saturated samples and detail already clipped in camera cannot be recovered.
LibRaw's output conversion clips negative RGB; this is not a full floating-point wide-gamut RAW development pipeline.
The 16-bit quarter-exposure output trades two bits of container precision for two stops of container headroom.
Half-size development changes demosaicing and pixel scale; matched comparisons must use the same decode.
